rounds.fact: About.com organized the web using human 'guides' who curated links on specific topics, a labor-intensive model for making sense of the internet before search engines got good enough to do it automatically.
Fox News launched its website alongside the cable channel in the mid-90s, and its early design leaned heavily on the bold red-white-and-blue branding that still defines the network today.
Plenty of Fish was famously built and run by a single person for years, supported entirely by ads, before eventually being sold for hundreds of millions of dollars.
Airbnb started in 2008 with the founders renting out air mattresses in their own apartment during a design conference, which is where the original name came from.
LinkedIn launched in 2003 out of a founder's living room. By 2005 it was already leaning into the dense, spreadsheet-like profile layout that professional networking sites still use.
